## 假日債市簡報

美國固定收益市場9月7日因勞動節休市，符合SIFMA的全日休市建議，當天並無美國固定收益市場的價格發現。假日期間最重要的新進展，是伊朗宣布與阿曼就荷姆茲海峽臨時航道的談判已接近達成協議。這為緩解能源供應中斷帶來一種可能，但尚不能證明通行已經恢復：船舶仍受到威脅，沙烏地阿拉伯能源設施據報遇襲，也讓供應紓解的前景更加複雜。美國下一個交易日的判斷關鍵，在於外交宣示能否轉化為實體供應的持續改善。

各國官方調整資產持有與流動性的決策，也將影響市場恢復交易後的走勢。日本公布外國證券持有額大幅下降，首相顧問也將預估的日本央行緊縮時點提前；印度則從討論如何吸收異常龐大的外幣流入，進展到大規模回收國內流動性。即使不考慮通膨，這些變化仍可能影響公債需求。借款人取得融資的情況也有明顯差異：有企業正籌備新融資，印度也完成了代幣化債券發行，但澳洲開發商僅獲針對部分業務的緊急支持，法國實驗室業者的貸款銀行則尋求退出。總體經濟方面，歐洲生產與房市數據疲弱，是制衡能源所帶來緊縮壓力的主要因素；不過，投資人信心回升，也使成長前景不能一概解讀為惡化。

## 全球利率、信用與主權動態

伊朗外交部發言人Esmail Baghaei表示，與阿曼的談判已進入最後階段，內容包括荷姆茲海峽的臨時安全航道安排。數艘空載的卡達液化天然氣船正返回波斯灣方向，可能是為恢復出口預作準備。這兩項進展都不足以證明商船已恢復不受限制的通行。伊朗仍警告船舶，在阿曼海岸附近有遭受攻擊的風險；另有報導指出，沙烏地阿拉伯位於紅海的石油設施遇襲，為能源運輸增添另一項威脅。Kpler記錄顯示，過去10天通過荷姆茲海峽的大宗商品船舶平均每天僅10艘，為5月以來最低。因此，擬議航道對政策的意義，取決於實際運輸量與安全狀況，而不只是談判能否完成。

供應中斷對企業現金流的衝擊並不一致，也會改變獲利在企業之間的分配。彭博取得的財務資料顯示，截至6月的六個月內，Gunvor獲利年增644%；Mercuria截至6月的九個月獲利則年增122%。這些數據顯示，大宗商品中介業者在戰爭造成的市場失衡中大幅獲利，但兩者財報涵蓋期間不同，不能視為衡量整個產業表現的共同基準。貿易商獲利增加之際，必須採購、運輸燃料的企業仍可能持續承壓；因此，貿易商獲利增加，並不足以證明央行面對的供應限制已經改善。

歐洲最新的經濟活動數據，進一步凸顯央行若以緊縮政策回應供應限制，可能付出的代價。德國7月工業生產下降1.1%，市場原預期增加0.1%。汽車產出下滑9.2%，德國汽車工業協會將其歸因於連續數週停產；能源生產在風力與太陽能發電支持下增加4.7%，營建產出也成長0.9%。降幅集中於汽車業，不能據此認定各工業部門都出現同等嚴重的萎縮。不過，萊茵河水位偏低，可能妨礙8月及9月的經濟活動；經濟學家也預期，工廠訂單增加要到第4季才會帶動生產。這意味著，若進一步收緊貨幣政策，工業部門可能在復甦持續延後之際，再承受緊縮壓力。

相較於實際數據，投資人的看法改善得快得多。9月歐元區Sentix指數從0.9升至5.1，高於市場共識的2.0，連續第五個月上升，並創2022年2月以來最高。現況指數由-8.0改善至-3.3，預期指數增加3.5點至13.8。德國綜合指數則從-11.9升至-2.8，連續第四個月回升，為2025年7月以來最佳。調查涵蓋1,052名投資人，其中209名為機構受訪者。投資人對未來經濟活動更有信心，但7月生產仍然下滑，歐洲利率因此同時受到眼前工業疲弱與未來復甦預期改善的牽動。至今也仍缺乏明確證據，顯示能源通膨正擴散至服務與薪資。

在經濟實況與信心分歧之際，德國的財政辯論也凸顯政策能否落實的重要性。薩克森－安哈特邦選舉後，總理梅爾茨表示，聯合政府必須改善合作，但政策目標不變。關鍵是舉債能有多大程度轉化為具生產效益的投資。Ifo估計，去年原本指定用於支出的新增債務，有95%實際上用來填補一般預算缺口。斯圖加特將2026年營業稅收入預估下修至7億歐元，遠低於2023年逾16億歐元的紀錄，並通過2009年以來首度撙節預算，顯示地方政府縮減支出可能抵銷全國性的刺激措施。5,000億歐元投資計畫有憲法保障，須取得三分之二多數才能推翻；UniCredit的Andreas Rees預期，改革較可能出現部分縮水或延後，而非陷入政治癱瘓。德國債務占GDP比率為64%，仍保有財政空間；但2027年計畫新增債務超過2,000億歐元，隨著債券供給增加，政策能否落實、舉債能帶來多少未來成長，也愈來愈重要。

英國則對公共舉債的用途提出更直接的承諾。財政大臣John Healey在首次重要演說中，重申財政紀律及與首相Andy Burnham的政策一致性，並提出運用國家財富基金與英國商業銀行，吸引區域投資。依財政規則，這些機構提供的貸款列為金融資產，檢核2029/30年度債務須下降的要求時，可用來抵銷舉債所增加的負債。因此，政府增加放貸，不會使按此規則衡量的債務狀況等額惡化，但新增債務的利息支出仍須計入，利息負擔並未消失。Healey提出的措施包括撥予英國商業銀行1.5億英鎊，以支持北部處於擴張階段的企業；提高地方留用所得稅收入的比例；以及承諾在2029年前將企業監管減少25%。這套做法並非推出大規模新支出方案，而是高度仰賴政策落實的改善，以及民間投資的帶動。

國內經濟為這項策略帶來阻力。捷豹路虎宣布計畫裁員最多4,000人。Lloyds公布8月房價年減0.4%，是2023年11月以來首次年減，市場原預期上漲0.2%；月比下跌0.2%，也不如預期的上漲0.1%，7月原公布上漲0.1%，則下修為下跌0.1%。凱投宏觀估計，近期市場利率上升，可能使一般2年期固定利率房貸的利率，從7月的4.8%升至9月接近5%。不過，房市數據並不一致：Nationwide公布8月房價年增1.6%、月增0.2%，另一項招聘調查也顯示，英國企業增加全職人員招募。融資成本上升正在壓抑部分需求，但尚不能據此認定就業或房市已全面萎縮。

法國財政調整面對的政治限制更加明確。國民聯盟主席Jordan Bardella承諾反對向家庭與企業加稅，縮小了尋求降低赤字的少數政府可採取的選項。Jean-Luc Melenchon新一輪對ECB緊縮的批評，聚焦衰退風險；此舉擴大了他與ECB的衝突，但並未產生新的債務註銷安排。Bardella也主張，不再無條件支持烏克蘭，改為更著重利益交換的關係。這些都是政治立場，而非已通過的財政或援助決策，但增加了國內財政整頓與對外支持能否持續的不確定性。

烏克蘭眼前的融資限制則更為具體。IMF代表團在基輔進行融資審查時，向國會議員明確表示，不應期待境外低價包裹課稅的必要條件能獲豁免。該法案將對價值低於150歐元、即$175的包裹課徵加值稅，但上週未能通過一讀。烏克蘭2026年預算赤字超過$320億，能否符合條件，關係到經濟運作與社會給付所需的資金。相較於烏克蘭既有的國際援助需求，這次審查訪問後更值得注意的是，IMF明確堅持放款條件，表明不應期待豁免。

日本最新公布的準備資產資料，顯示官方可能是外國債券的賣方；這與民間投資人因國內殖利率而重新考慮配置，是兩件不同的事。財務省週一公布，8月外國證券持有額減少$878億，創歷來最大降幅，規模接近近期匯市干預金額。分析師推測，日本可能出售了包括較短天期美國公債在內的證券，為支撐日圓籌資。目前可以確認的是持有額下降，至於出售哪些證券、出於何種目的，仍屬分析師的解讀，不能據此認定日本投資人普遍撤出外國債券。

至於政府周邊對貨幣政策的態度，首相高市早苗的經濟顧問、法國農業信貸銀行日本首席經濟學家會田卓司的預測修正，提供了另一項變化的線索。他將預估的日本央行下一次升息時間，從2027年1月提前至9月，認為可把握10月初臨時國會會期開始前的短暫時機升息。他預期明年1月前還會再升息一次，之後回到大約每半年調整一次的步調。這項修正出自一位具代表性的再通膨派顧問，意味政府周邊對政策正常化的阻力可能減弱；不過，財務大臣片山皋月重申，決策權在日本央行。此外，據報市場也有停損交易被觸發，並有選擇權交易商賣出美元，因此假日期間的外匯需求，不能全數歸因於投資人對基本面的新判斷。

觀察這類官方資金流向時，紐約聯準銀行的研究提供了較完整的背景，有助於避免過度解讀。去年美元占全球外匯準備的56%，低於十年前的64%；但研究人員Linda Goldberg與Sneha Parthasarathy發現，在2015年以來的兩個研究期間，增加與減少美元持有額的國家數量大致相當。2015至2019年主動分散配置的變動主要來自中國與俄羅斯；2019至2023年則多由中國、俄羅斯、墨西哥及摩洛哥帶動。其他國家的配置，仍多與匯率管理及取得美元流動性的需求有關。另一份6月研究發現，各國普遍有意長期降低美元曝險，但這類意向仍須與實際發生的交易區分。特定國家出售準備資產可能影響美國公債的承接，卻不足以證明各國官方普遍迴避美元。

印度的情況顯示，外匯操作可以在強化對外緩衝的同時，回收國內資金。印度央行9月7日吸收超過6兆盧比，約合$635.3億。銀行先在目標吸收7兆盧比的30天期操作中投放2.59兆盧比，之後再於隔夜操作投標3.53兆盧比。五名交易員將30天期參與偏弱歸因於技術問題；一名熟悉操作的人士則反駁，表示所有投標都已透過e-Kuber送達。由於雙方說法不一，尚不能將投標不足認定為銀行業刻意不參與沖銷操作。9月6日銀行體系流動性已達11.6兆盧比，接近存款的4%；因此，儘管這次回收規模可觀，仍不能據此認定過剩流動性已經消失。

印度央行也在進行流動性標售的同時賣出美元。六名銀行人士估計，截至9月4日的一週內，央行至少賣出$80億，最高估計達$150億；其中一人估計為$100億至$110億，至少是前一週的三倍。賣出美元除了支撐本幣，也會回收盧比。在此之前，印度針對海外借款及外幣存款提供特殊避險優惠，吸引逾$1,360億資金，這是理解異常龐大過剩流動性的重要背景。印度央行回收的資金已超過8.5兆盧比，IDFC First Bank則指出，市場穩定計畫債券及先賣後買換匯交易，可能是後續工具。採用哪種工具，將決定沖銷操作是增加政府債券供給，還是更多透過外匯與貨幣市場進行。

中國對金融機構的資本挹注，正從銀行擴及保險業。在先前公布的增資計畫中，五家國有保險公司將合計獲得人民幣700億元，其中中國人壽為人民幣350億元、中國太平為人民幣70億元；中國人保則計畫向財政部定向增發最多人民幣150億元A股。這是首次以特別國債籌資支持保險公司，將過去用於銀行的工具延伸至保險業。GMF Research估計，投入四家商業保險公司的人民幣600億元，可支持約人民幣1,000億元的新增股票曝險。因此，充實保險業資本不僅提高對債權人的保障，也可能改變保險公司的資產配置能力，這些資金未必全數用於加碼債券。另一方面，中國8月外匯存底從$3.419兆升至$3.438兆，高於市場共識的$3.425兆。外匯存底增加、對外緩衝擴大之際，8月美元也走弱，僅憑存底上升，無法判定是否新買進了準備資產或買進哪些資產。

投資活動也在帶動民間資金流入。馬來西亞8月政府債券與公司債吸引$39億外資，為馬來西亞國家銀行自2016年開始統計以來最高單月金額。RBC的Abbas Keshvani將需求與出口成長，以及該國資料中心產業相關的外國直接投資連結。不過，馬來西亞尚未拍板的科技選擇，也可能影響這項資金流入的支撐因素：馬來西亞正評估在20億令吉、約合$4.94億的主權AI計畫中使用華為Ascend 910C晶片，並已選定具國家背景的馬來西亞電訊擔任營運商。美國政府警告，使用這些晶片可能違反美國出口規範。馬來西亞視此為商業選擇，並正在討論另一輪招標，可能讓輝達更直接參與競爭。目前尚未確定最終採用華為。關鍵在於，馬來西亞追求科技自主時，能否維繫帶來這些資金的美國投資關係。

澳洲則面對類似投資帶來的另一種後果。彭博經濟研究的James McIntyre估計，資料中心資本支出在2026至2027年可能超過GDP的2%，加劇與住宅、基礎建設及再生能源計畫爭奪熟練營建人力的情況。CreditorWatch的Ivan Colhoun認為，隨之而來的材料與薪資壓力，使疲弱房市指標對貨幣政策的參考價值低於平常。資料中心投資的生產力效益可能稍後才會出現，營建需求卻先到來；未來生產能力可望提高，並不等於當下通膨壓力就會下降。

企業交易顯示，發行人正透過不同市場接觸投資人，而非依賴單一融資管道。Uber委任高盛、法國巴黎銀行、美國銀行、德意志銀行與摩根士丹利，籌備可能的首次歐元債發行，規劃分為3、6、8、12及20年期五檔固定利率債券。在Uber擴張歐洲業務、包括已同意以$148億收購Delivery Hero之際，這項準備可拓寬融資選項。今年美國企業與金融機構已發行近1,250億歐元的歐元債，發行速度創紀錄。因此，即使Uber尚未確定規模或定價，發行人之間爭取歐洲投資人資金的競爭已值得關注。

MTN與國際債券投資人的接觸，則尚未指向特定交易。Absa、美國銀行、花旗與MUFG上週安排了倫敦會議，是MTN十年未在國際市場發債後，首次進行這類準備。公司將會議定位為業績更新，路演也明確不涉及交易。MTN表示，有足夠資源償還10月到期、剩餘$5億的歐洲債券；另擬以約$22億收購尚未持有的IHS Towers股份，則構成另一筆資金需求。管理階層曾表示，收購將部分以債務融資。因此，MTN接觸投資人，是為日後進入市場籌資保留選項，尚不能據此認定公司有迫切的再融資缺口，或已完成債券發售。

相較於上述融資準備，印度已有一筆交易完成發行。國營電力融資機構REC透過2028年5月到期、票息7.30%的代幣化票據，籌得50億盧比，約合$5,290萬，進度已從先前徵求投標推進至完成發行。約20名投資人使用印度央行數位貨幣參與，據報買方包括HDFC Bank與ICICI Bank。其他具名參與者包括Axis Bank、Yes Bank、AK Capital Services、ICICI Securities Primary Dealership、Taurus Group與Trust Investment Advisors。Taurus與AK Capital確認參與；HDFC確認安排發行，但未評論是否買進。將區塊鏈證券與央行數位支付連結，可望加快配售與交割，但單憑這次完成發行，尚不能證明次級市場交易深度增加。傳統債市方面，Reliance Industries正籌備發行最多1,250億盧比、約合$13億的本地債券，可能成為印度今年規模最大的上市債券交易。

財務陷入困境的借款人，能否繼續獲得融資，則更取決於個別條件。Bathla管理人Teneo與五家貸款機構達成緊急資金支持協議，讓部分營運維持兩週。一名熟悉協議的人士表示，金額約為400萬澳元，但Teneo未予確認。只有與參與貸款機構相關的工程會繼續，其餘計畫暫停，約213名員工停止工作。Bathla欠債權人34億澳元，這筆新資金只能為公司爭取時間、保護特定工程，並非用來支應整個集團完成所有計畫。更長期的支持，仍須與更廣泛的貸款機構達成協議。

Cerba的最新進展，同樣在於債權人是否願意繼續承擔曝險，而非新一輪重整公告。這家由EQT支持的實驗室集團正朝協商和解程序推進，一家或多家銀行尋求出售其4.5億歐元循環信用額度中、約2,800萬歐元的債權。這類額度的交易頻率低於債券，出售後，與借款人協商問題債權的工作可能從往來銀行轉由專業基金承接。相較於Cerba約50億歐元的債務負擔，擬出售金額雖不大，卻具體顯示已有貸款機構在重整推進期間考慮退出。

## 下一交易時段觀察

通膨方面，關鍵是航運若有改善，能否持續到足以在成本壓力進一步擴散前，使其緩和。伊朗與阿曼的安排，若伴隨船舶持續通行及攻擊減少，才會更具實質意義；若只有協議而沒有這些變化，能源供應限制仍然存在。加拿大預定9月8日對數百項美國產品加徵15%至50%關稅，帶來另一項潛在成本衝擊。9月10日ECB決策與同日美國PPI，以及9月11日CPI，將有助於判斷需要多大程度的貨幣緊縮，才能因應這些壓力。相較於市場預期ECB升息25個基點至2.5%，ECB如何評估第二輪效應，對後續政策路徑更有參考價值。非能源通膨若擴散，將支持進一步緊縮；若持續溫和，則仍有空間區分燃料衝擊與持續性的國內通膨。

美國恢復交易後，公債需求須與通膨壓力分開觀察。日本公布準備資產資料後，9月8日美國3年期公債標售與9月9日10年期標售，將呈現市場對不同利率敏感度債券的需求。若投標疲弱，官方出售外國證券及公司債發行爭取資金的競爭，影響就會更大；若市場順利承接，則不宜立即將這些變化解讀為供給壓力。接著，9月17至18日日本央行會議，將檢驗會田卓司提前正常化的預測，包括政策展望是否讓日本投資人有更強的誘因將資金留在國內。他修正預測，不代表這類投資組合調整已經發生。

烏克蘭能否符合融資條件，則須依其立法時程觀察。國會稅務委員會主席Danylo Hetmantsev表示，政府計畫9月7日重新提交包裹加值稅法案，於下一週再度爭取國會通過。法案若通過，將滿足IMF的一項明確要求，提高預算融資持續獲得支持的可能；若再度失敗，烏克蘭仍有資金需求，卻無法滿足貸款方條件的困境就會延續。即使能源供應改善、全球債券需求保持有序，這項結果仍可能改變烏克蘭的主權融資風險。
zh-TW.methodology_note: SIFMA建議美國固定收益市場於勞動節全日休市；前一交易日的市場水準不作為當日行情變動。

overall_summary.headline: 荷姆茲臨時航道可望紓解供應，但仍待落實；官方資產與流動性調整增添美國開市變數
overall_summary.session_narrative:
美國固定收益市場因勞動節休市，假日期間的進展將留待下一個交易日評估。伊朗表示，與阿曼就荷姆茲臨時航道的談判已接近達成協議，空載的卡達液化天然氣船也正返回波斯灣方向。然而，船舶仍受到威脅，沙烏地阿拉伯能源設施據報持續遭到攻擊。過去10天，大宗商品船舶平均每天僅通行10艘，外交進展尚未證明實體供應已獲紓解。

日本公布8月外國證券持有額減少$878億，創歷來最大降幅；分析師將其與支撐日圓連結，但這不足以證明日本投資人普遍撤出。另一項可能影響未來需求的因素，是政府顧問將預估的日本央行緊縮時點提前。印度央行9月7日回收超過6兆盧比，從討論如何因應異常資金流入，進展至大規模吸收流動性；後續措施可能增加政府債券供給，也可能透過外匯市場進行。

歐洲的成長數據，使利率前景不能單純朝緊縮方向解讀。德國7月生產下滑1.1%，降幅集中於汽車業；歐元區Sentix信心指數卻從0.9升至5.1。英國房市數據相互矛盾，對需求放緩的判斷同樣須有所保留。財政投資計畫仍受政策落實與融資成本制約。企業取得融資的情況也不一致：Uber籌備可能的歐元融資，REC完成代幣化票據發行；Bathla卻僅取得限於特定工程的短期支持，Cerba的貸款機構則尋求出售問題債權。IMF堅持包裹加值稅要求，也使烏克蘭面對一項獨立的融資限制。

日本公布準備資產資料後，美國公債標售將檢驗市場承接能力；ECB決策與美國通膨數據，則將檢驗能源成本是否正擴散為更廣泛的通膨。
overall_summary.summary: 航運若能持續恢復，可望緩和能源壓力，但歐洲經濟活動轉弱尚未化解通膨與成長之間的政策取捨；準備資產出售與流動性回收，也可能獨立影響公債需求。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Holiday Fixed-Income Brief

U.S. fixed-income markets were closed for Labor Day on September 7, consistent with SIFMA's full-close recommendation. There was no same-day U.S. fixed-income price discovery. The principal change during the holiday information window was Iran's announcement that negotiations with Oman were nearing agreement on a temporary shipping route through the Strait of Hormuz. That creates a possible route toward easing the energy disruption, but not yet evidence of restored passage: threats against vessels continued, and reports of attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure complicated the prospect of relief. For the next U.S. session, the important distinction is between a diplomatic announcement and a sustained improvement in physical supply.

Official balance-sheet decisions provide a separate influence on the reopening. Japan disclosed a large reduction in foreign securities, while an adviser to its prime minister brought forward his Bank of Japan tightening forecast. India moved from discussing how to absorb exceptional foreign-currency inflows to withdrawing domestic liquidity on a substantial scale. These developments could affect demand for government debt independently of inflation. Financing access also remains differentiated: new corporate funding preparations and a completed Indian tokenized bond contrast with selective emergency support for an Australian developer and lenders seeking an exit from French laboratory debt. Weak European production and housing readings are the main macroeconomic counterweight to energy-led tightening pressure, although stronger investor confidence prevents a uniform growth-deterioration interpretation.

## Global Rates, Credit, And Sovereign Developments

Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei said negotiations with Oman were in their final stages, including arrangements for a temporary safe route through Hormuz. Several empty Qatari LNG tankers were heading back toward the Persian Gulf, potentially positioning for renewed exports. Neither development establishes that unrestricted commercial passage has resumed. Tehran continued to warn vessels about attack risk near Oman's coastline, while reports of strikes on Saudi Arabian oil infrastructure on the Red Sea introduced a separate threat to energy transport. Kpler recorded an average of only 10 commodity ships a day through Hormuz over the preceding 10 days, the lowest since May. The policy significance of the proposed route therefore depends on actual throughput and security, not simply the completion of negotiations.

For borrowers, disruption also redistributes earnings rather than imposing an identical cash-flow shock. Financial data seen by Bloomberg showed Gunvor's profit increasing 644% year over year in the six months through June and Mercuria's rising 122% in the nine months through June. These different reporting periods demonstrate substantial gains for commodity intermediaries amid the war's dislocations, not a common measure of industry performance. Stronger trading-house earnings can coexist with persistent pressure on companies that must purchase and transport fuel; they do not establish an improvement in the supply constraint confronting central banks.

Fresh European activity data make the cost of responding to that constraint clearer. German industrial production fell 1.1% in July against expectations for a 0.1% increase. Automotive output declined 9.2%, which the German Automotive Association attributed to a multi-week production shutdown, while energy production increased 4.7% with support from wind and solar generation and construction rose 0.9%. The concentration of the decline in autos limits the inference of an equally severe contraction across industry. Nevertheless, low Rhine water levels could impede August and September activity, and economists did not expect stronger factory orders to lift production before Q4. Additional monetary restraint could consequently reach an industrial economy whose recovery remains delayed.

Investor assessments improved much faster than that hard-data picture. September's euro-area Sentix index rose to 5.1 from 0.9, exceeding the 2.0 consensus, recording a fifth consecutive increase and reaching its highest since February 2022. Current conditions improved to -3.3 from -8.0, while expectations increased 3.5 points to 13.8. Germany's headline rose to -2.8 from -11.9, its fourth consecutive gain and strongest reading since July 2025. The survey covered 1,052 investors, including 209 institutional respondents. This is evidence of greater confidence in prospective activity, not a reversal of July's production result. It leaves European rates exposed to competing horizons: immediate industrial weakness and an improving expectation of recovery, with limited clear evidence so far that energy inflation is broadening into services and wages.

Germany's fiscal debate adds an implementation issue to that divergence. After the Saxony-Anhalt election, Chancellor Friedrich Merz said his coalition needed to work better while maintaining its objectives. The question is how effectively borrowing becomes productive investment. Ifo estimated that 95% of new debt earmarked for spending last year instead filled holes in the regular budget. Stuttgart has cut its 2026 trade-tax projection to EUR700 million from a 2023 record above EUR1.6 billion and adopted its first austerity budget since 2009, showing how local retrenchment can offset national stimulus. The EUR500 billion investment program is constitutionally anchored and would require a two-thirds majority to unravel; UniCredit's Andreas Rees expected some dilution or delay in reforms rather than political paralysis. Germany's 64% debt-to-GDP ratio preserves fiscal capacity, but more than EUR200 billion of planned new debt for 2027 makes delivery increasingly important to the relationship between additional supply and future growth.

Britain supplied a more direct commitment on the use of public borrowing. In his first major speech, Chancellor John Healey reaffirmed fiscal discipline and alignment with Prime Minister Andy Burnham, while proposing to use the National Wealth Fund and British Business Bank to attract regional investment. Under the fiscal rules, loans made through these institutions are financial assets that offset the borrowing liability for the debt-falling requirement in 2029/30; the additional servicing cost still counts. That treatment can accommodate lending without an equivalent deterioration in the measured debt position, but it does not remove the interest bill. Healey's measures included GBP150 million for the British Business Bank to support northern scale-ups, greater local retention of income tax and a commitment to reduce business regulation by 25% by 2029. The approach relies heavily on improving delivery and mobilizing private investment, rather than announcing a large new spending package.

The domestic economy presents obstacles to that strategy. Jaguar Land Rover announced plans to cut as many as 4,000 jobs. Lloyds reported that house prices fell 0.4% year over year in August, the first annual decline since November 2023, against expectations for a 0.2% increase. Prices fell 0.2% on the month rather than rising 0.1%, and July's initial 0.1% gain was revised to a 0.1% decline. Capital Economics estimated that recent market-rate increases could bring a typical two-year fixed mortgage rate toward 5% in September from 4.8% in July. The housing evidence is not unanimous: Nationwide reported 1.6% annual growth and a 0.2% monthly rise for August, while a separate hiring survey showed British companies increasing full-time recruitment. Higher financing costs are restraining parts of demand without yet establishing a comprehensive employment or housing contraction.

Political constraints on fiscal adjustment became more explicit in France. National Rally president Jordan Bardella pledged to oppose tax increases on households and businesses, narrowing the options available to a minority government seeking to reduce the deficit. Jean-Luc Melenchon's new criticism of ECB tightening focused on recession risk; it widened his confrontation with the institution without creating a new debt-cancellation arrangement. Bardella also advocated replacing unconditional support for Ukraine with a more transactional relationship. These are political positions, not enacted fiscal or aid decisions, but they increase uncertainty about the durability of both domestic consolidation and external support.

Ukraine's immediate financing constraint is more concrete. An IMF mission conducting a funding review in Kyiv made clear to lawmakers that an exception should not be expected for the required tax on low-value parcels from abroad. The bill would impose VAT on parcels worth under EUR150, or $175, and failed its first reading the previous week. With a 2026 budget deficit exceeding $32 billion, compliance matters to funding for the economy and social payments. The changed information is the firmness of the lender's condition following its review visit, not merely another statement that Ukraine needs international assistance.

Japan's new reserve disclosure identifies an official source of foreign-bond supply distinct from private investors reconsidering domestic yields. Finance Ministry data released Monday showed foreign-securities holdings falling a record $87.8 billion in August, close to the scale of recent currency intervention. Analysts inferred that Japan probably sold securities, including shorter-maturity Treasuries, to finance support for the yen. The holdings change is observed; the instrument selection and purpose remain an interpretation. It should not be read as proof of a general Japanese investor withdrawal from foreign bonds.

Takuji Aida, an economic adviser to Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Credit Agricole's chief Japan economist, supplied a separate change in the policy coalition. He advanced his next BOJ increase forecast from January 2027 to September, identifying a narrow opportunity before an extraordinary parliamentary session in early October. He expected another increase by January and then a return to approximately semiannual moves. Coming from a prominent reflationist adviser, that revision suggests less resistance to normalization near the government, although Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama reiterated that decisions belong to the BOJ. Reports of stop-loss execution and options dealers selling dollars also show why currency demand during the holiday cannot be assigned entirely to a new fundamental decision.

A New York Fed study offers useful discipline in interpreting such official flows. The dollar accounted for 56% of currency reserves last year versus 64% a decade earlier, but researchers Linda Goldberg and Sneha Parthasarathy found roughly equal numbers of countries increasing and decreasing dollar holdings in two periods since 2015. China and Russia accounted for most active diversification in 2015-2019; China, Russia, Mexico and Morocco drove much of it in 2019-2023. Exchange-rate management and access to dollar liquidity remained important explanations elsewhere. A separate June study found widespread intentions to reduce dollar exposure over the long term, but intentions and realized transactions measure different things. Specific reserve sales can matter for Treasury absorption without establishing universal official dollar avoidance.

India illustrates how currency operations can simultaneously strengthen an external buffer and withdraw domestic cash. The RBI absorbed more than 6 trillion rupees, or $63.53 billion, on September 7. Banks offered 3.53 trillion rupees in an overnight operation after placing 2.59 trillion in a 30-day operation that had targeted 7 trillion. Five traders attributed the weak 30-day participation to technical problems; a person familiar with the operation disputed that account and said all bids passed through e-Kuber. The shortfall therefore cannot confidently be treated as a deliberate banking-sector rejection of sterilization. System liquidity had reached 11.6 trillion rupees on September 6, close to 4% of deposits, so the completed drain is consequential without implying that the surplus has disappeared.

Dollar sales are operating alongside those liquidity auctions. Six bankers estimated that the RBI sold at least $8 billion in the week through September 4, with estimates ranging to $15 billion; one placed the amount at $10 billion-$11 billion, at least three times the preceding week's figure. Such sales withdraw rupees as well as supporting the currency. They follow more than $136 billion attracted through exceptional hedging incentives for overseas borrowing and foreign-currency deposits, the minimum context needed to explain the unusually large surplus. RBI withdrawals had exceeded 8.5 trillion rupees, while IDFC First Bank identified Market Stabilisation Scheme bonds and sell-buy swaps as possible further instruments. Their use would determine whether sterilization adds government-paper supply or works more through the currency and money markets.

Capital support in China is reaching a new class of financial institution. Within the previously announced recapitalization, five state insurers are set to receive a combined 70 billion yuan, including 35 billion for China Life and 7 billion for China Taiping; PICC plans an A-share placement of up to 15 billion yuan to the Finance Ministry. This is the first use of special-bond financing to support insurers, extending a tool previously used for banks. GMF Research estimated that 60 billion yuan going to four commercial insurers could support approximately 100 billion yuan of additional equity exposure. Stronger insurer capital can therefore alter asset-allocation capacity as well as creditor protection; it need not translate entirely into additional bond purchases. Separately, China's August FX reserves increased to $3.438 trillion from $3.419 trillion, above the $3.425 trillion consensus. The larger external buffer coincided with dollar weakness during August and does not by itself identify new reserve-asset purchases.

Private capital is also arriving through investment-led channels. Malaysia received $3.9 billion of foreign inflows into government and corporate bonds in August, the largest monthly amount in Bank Negara Malaysia data beginning in 2016. RBC's Abbas Keshvani linked demand to export growth and foreign direct investment associated with the country's data-center industry. A prospective technology choice complicates that support: Malaysia is evaluating Huawei Ascend 910C chips for a 2 billion-ringgit, or $494 million, sovereign-AI initiative, with state-linked Telekom Malaysia selected as operator. Washington has warned that use of those chips could violate U.S. export rules. Malaysia regards its choice as commercial and is discussing another tender that could permit more direct competition from Nvidia. No final Huawei selection has been established. The issue is whether technological autonomy can be pursued without damaging the American investment relationships supporting the financing story.

Australia faces a different consequence from similar investment. Bloomberg Economics' James McIntyre estimated that data-center capital expenditure could exceed 2% of GDP in 2026-27, intensifying competition for skilled construction labor with housing, infrastructure and renewable-energy projects. CreditorWatch's Ivan Colhoun argued that associated pressure on materials and wages makes softer housing indicators less informative for monetary policy than usual. Productivity benefits could emerge later, but construction demand arrives first. That sequence distinguishes an eventual increase in productive capacity from an immediate reduction in inflation pressure.

Corporate transactions show investors being approached through different markets rather than a single financing channel. Uber mandated Goldman Sachs, BNP Paribas, Bank of America, Deutsche Bank and Morgan Stanley for a possible debut five-part euro bond, with fixed-rate maturities of 3, 6, 8, 12 and 20 years. The preparation broadens its funding options as it expands in Europe, including its agreed $14.8 billion purchase of Delivery Hero. Nearly EUR125 billion of euro bonds have already been sold this year by U.S. corporate and financial issuers, a record pace that makes competition for European investors relevant even before Uber fixes a size or price.

MTN's contact with international bondholders is less transaction-specific. Absa, Bank of America, Citigroup and MUFG organized London meetings last week, its first such preparation after a decade without international issuance. The company described the meetings as an earnings update, and the roadshow was explicitly non-deal. MTN says it has sufficient resources to repay its remaining $500 million Eurobond due in October, while its proposed roughly $2.2 billion purchase of the IHS Towers shares it does not already own creates a separate cash requirement. Management has said debt would partly finance that acquisition. Investor outreach therefore creates an option for market access rather than demonstrating an urgent refinancing shortfall or a completed bond sale.

India supplied a completed financing rather than another proposal. State power lender REC raised 5 billion rupees, or $52.9 million, through tokenized notes due in May 2028 at a 7.30% coupon, moving beyond its earlier solicitation of bids. About 20 investors participated using the RBI's digital currency, with HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank among the reported buyers. Other named participants included Axis Bank, Yes Bank, AK Capital Services, ICICI Securities Primary Dealership, Taurus Group and Trust Investment Advisors. Taurus and AK Capital confirmed participation; HDFC confirmed arranging the issue without commenting on a purchase. Connecting blockchain securities to central-bank digital payments offers a route to faster allotment and settlement, although the completed placement alone does not demonstrate deeper secondary trading. At the conventional end of the market, Reliance Industries is preparing up to 125 billion rupees, or $1.3 billion, of local bonds, potentially India's largest listed transaction this year.

Where borrowers are distressed, continued financing is much more selective. Bathla administrator Teneo agreed emergency support with five lenders to keep limited operations running for two weeks. A person familiar with the agreement put it at approximately A$4 million; Teneo did not confirm the amount. Only construction associated with participating lenders would continue, while other projects were suspended and about 213 employees stopped work. Against A$3.4 billion owed to creditors, the new money buys time and protects selected projects rather than funding completion across the group. Longer-term support still requires agreement with the broader lender base.

Cerba's latest development similarly concerns which creditors remain exposed, not a new announcement of its restructuring. One or more banks are seeking to sell approximately EUR28 million of its EUR450 million revolving credit facility as the EQT-backed laboratory group proceeds toward conciliation. Such facilities trade less frequently than bonds; a sale can transfer the work of negotiating a distressed claim from a relationship bank to a specialist fund. The proposed disposal is small relative to Cerba's approximately EUR5 billion debt burden, but it is concrete evidence of lenders considering an exit while the restructuring develops.

## Next Open-Session Watch

The central inflation question is whether any improvement in shipping becomes durable enough to ease cost pressure before it spreads more broadly. An Iran-Oman arrangement would be more consequential if accompanied by sustained vessel passage and fewer attacks; an agreement without those changes would leave the energy constraint intact. Canada's scheduled September 8 tariffs of 15%-50% on hundreds of U.S. products introduce another potential cost shock. The ECB's September 10 decision and U.S. PPI that day, followed by CPI on September 11, will test how much monetary restraint those pressures require. The expected 25-basis-point ECB increase to 2.5% is less informative for the subsequent path than its assessment of second-round effects. Broadening non-energy inflation would support further tightening; continued moderation would preserve room to distinguish a fuel shock from persistent domestic inflation.

Government-debt absorption is a separate test as U.S. trading resumes. The September 8 Treasury 3-year auction and September 9 10-year sale will reveal demand across different interest-rate exposures after Japan's reserve disclosure. Weak bidding would make official foreign-securities sales and competition from corporate issuance more consequential; orderly absorption would limit the immediate supply interpretation. The BOJ's September 17-18 meeting then tests Aida's accelerated normalization forecast, including whether the policy outlook offers Japanese investors a stronger reason to retain funds domestically. His revised view is not evidence that such portfolio changes have already occurred.

Ukraine's funding condition has its own timetable. Parliamentary tax-committee chair Danylo Hetmantsev said the government planned to resubmit the parcel-VAT bill on September 7 for another parliamentary attempt the following week. Passage would address a specific IMF requirement and improve the prospect of continued budget financing; another failure would prolong the gap between the country's funding needs and compliance with lender conditions. That outcome can change sovereign financing risk even if energy supply improves and global bond demand remains orderly.

section_summaries.summary: The Hormuz proposal changes the prospect of relief, not the evidence of restored passage. Japan's reserve disclosure points to possible official selling rather than a broad investor withdrawal, while India's completed liquidity drain turns a proposed response to inflows into action. Weak European activity restrains the tightening case, but improved confidence limits claims of uniform deterioration.

China's insurer support may fund equities, while Malaysia's record bond inflows face technology-policy risk and Australian data centers add cost pressure. overall_summary.headline: Proposed Hormuz route offers conditional relief as official balance-sheet shifts complicate the U.S. reopening
overall_summary.session_narrative:
U.S. fixed-income markets were closed for Labor Day, leaving the holiday's developments to be assessed at the next open session. Iran said negotiations with Oman on a temporary Hormuz route were nearing agreement, and empty Qatari LNG tankers were returning toward the Gulf. Yet threats to vessels and reported attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure persisted. Commodity traffic averaged only 10 ships a day over the preceding 10 days: diplomacy has not yet established physical supply relief.

Japan disclosed a record $87.8 billion August reduction in foreign securities, which analysts linked to yen support without establishing a general Japanese investor retreat. A government adviser's earlier BOJ tightening forecast adds a separate prospective influence on demand. India's RBI withdrew more than 6 trillion rupees on September 7, moving from discussion of exceptional inflows to substantial liquidity absorption; further measures could add government-paper supply or operate through currency markets.

European growth evidence limits a simple tightening interpretation. German July production fell 1.1%, concentrated in autos, while euro-area Sentix confidence rose to 5.1 from 0.9. Conflicting British housing readings likewise qualify the demand slowdown. Fiscal investment plans still depend on delivery and financing costs. Corporate access remains selective: Uber prepared possible euro funding and REC completed tokenized notes, while Bathla secured only temporary, project-specific support and Cerba lenders sought to sell distressed exposure. Ukraine faces a distinct financing constraint as the IMF holds firm on parcel VAT.

Treasury auctions will test debt absorption after the reserve disclosure; the ECB decision and U.S. inflation releases will test whether energy costs are spreading into broader inflation.
overall_summary.summary: A sustained recovery in shipping could ease energy pressure, but weaker European activity has yet to resolve the inflation trade-off, while reserve sales and liquidity withdrawals could independently affect government-bond demand.
